title: Manage supply chain risk throughout acquisition and operation: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: What assurance evidence is proportionate for this supplier, component, update path, or hardware trust claim?
focalInsight: Assurance combines provenance, scoped assessment, enforceable terms, lifecycle monitoring, technical verification, and exit.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Risk Management
nodes.decision: Set assurance depth from criticality, access, data, support.
nodes.failureExample: Brand is treated as safe lifecycle.

nodes.label: Supplier Risk
nodes.definition: Risk from provider practice, viability, access, subcontractors, change.
nodes.detail: Risk from provider practice, viability, access, subcontractors, change.
nodes.decision: Assess capability, scope, location, evidence, exit.

nodes.label: Third Party Assessment
nodes.failureExample: One-region report covers all services claim.

nodes.label: Service Level Agreement
nodes.decision: Set service, report, remedy, ownership, exit.

nodes.label: Software Bill of Materials
nodes.decision: Use for visibility, response, upgrade, ownership.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: It says what exists, not trust.

altSummary: Assurance combines provenance, scoped assessment, enforceable terms, lifecycle monitoring, technical verification, and exit.
textFallback:
supply chain risk management: Risk management for suppliers/products/components/delivery/updates. Decide: Set assurance depth from criticality, access, data, support. Example/failure: Brand is treated as safe lifecycle. Retrieve: SCRM spans dependency lifecycle.
supplier risk: Risk from provider practice, viability, access, subcontractors, change. Decide: Assess capability, scope, location, evidence, exit. Example/failure: Subcontractor changes unreviewed. Retrieve: Risk continues after selection.
product tampering: Unauthorized alteration of product/artifact/delivery. Decide: Verify provenance, integrity, signing, custody. Example/failure: Modified installer comes from mirror. Retrieve: Control origin and verification.
counterfeit: Component falsely claimed genuine/approved. Decide: Use authorized source and traceability. Example/failure: Cheap module has unknown firmware. Retrieve: Counterfeit is provenance failure.
malicious implant: Hidden hardware/firmware/software capability. Decide: Assess privileged interfaces, verification, monitoring. Example/failure: Backdoor gains remote admin. Retrieve: Implant needs lifecycle assurance.
third party assessment: Proportionate supplier/service evidence review. Decide: Match method/scope to criticality/data/access. Example/failure: One-region report covers all services claim. Retrieve: Evidence only supports its scope.
security requirements: Minimum supplier/product security outcomes. Decide: Make measurable, agreed, monitored, remedied. Example/failure: Contract says secure only. Retrieve: Requirements make assurance testable.
service level agreement: Contractual service performance commitments. Decide: Set service, report, remedy, ownership, exit. Example/failure: SLA excludes critical dependency. Retrieve: SLA covers actual reliance.
software bill of materials: Inventory of software components/dependencies. Decide: Use for visibility, response, upgrade, ownership. Example/failure: SBOM claimed to prove safety. Retrieve: It says what exists, not trust.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: What assurance evidence is proportionate for this supplier, component, update path, or hardware trust claim?
learningContract.misconception: A known vendor, SBOM, PUF, or silicon label by itself establishes trustworthy supply.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned rows expose distinctions, decision criteria, and misuse consequences.
learningContract.focalInsight: Assurance combines provenance, scoped assessment, enforceable terms, lifecycle monitoring, technical verification, and exit.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Implementation settings and jurisdiction-specific conclusions are not inferred from these concise concept comparisons.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: For a component claim, state required source, verification, lifecycle, monitoring, and response evidence.
